sentences.text: [3.0] By way of these petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution of India read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "CrPC"), the petitioners - accused have prayed to quash and set aside the complaint dated 28.06.2012 resulting into M. Case No.4 of 2012 for the offences punishable under Sections 120(B), 468, 471, 406, 420, 166, 167 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short "IPC") as well as order dated 28.06.2012 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajpipla in Misc. Criminal Case No.23/2012 and all the consequential proceedings arising therefrom.

[4.0] Learned advocates for the respective parties submitted that during the pendency of proceedings, the parties have settled the dispute amicably and pursuant to such mutual settlement,
the original complainant has also filed an undertaking dated 06.10.2024 which is taken on record.

In the undertaking, the original complainant has categorically stated that the dispute with the petitioners has been resolved amicably and he is ready to accept the demand draft for an amount of Rs.17,77,000/- and that he has no objection, if the present proceedings are quashed and set aside since there is no surviving grievance between them.

[5.0] It is the case of the petitioners that original accused Nos.1 to 5 are the government officers,
accused No.6 is the officer of NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/2092/2012 ORDER DATED:
09/10/2024 undefined insurance company and accused No.7 is the insurance company.

The Central Government of India floated Nationalized Scheme for the poor and lower strata of society holding BPL Card to ensure proper insurance and coverage under the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana (RSBY) and under the said scheme various hospitals were empanelled by ICICI Lombard for extension of the said benefits under the control and supervision of the State Government and accused Nos.1 to 5 were the members and under the helm of the said committee, government was imparting the said health services.

Under the said scheme, hospital of respondent No.2 - original complainant came to be empanelled and under the scheme, respondent No.2 had executed the MoU with the ICICI Lombard to extend the benefits of the scheme.
Under the MoU, hospital used to provide identification of beneficiaries and terms and conditions were decided and there was some obligation on the part of the hospitals.

It is alleged that in collusion and connivance of accused persons, they have forged the document with a view to avoid the legitimate claims raised by respondent No.2 - original complainant and for that he has raised the grievance before the authority.
The authority has examined the claims and ultimately it was found that with a view to avoid the payment for financial year 2010-11, the hospital was de-empanelled.

Then, respondent No.2 has raised the grievance upto higher authority and Central Government and ultimately it was found that the claims raised by respondent No.2 were genuine and at the instance and in connivance and collusion of accused persons, they have forged NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/2092/2012 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined the documents of pathology reports and alleged irregularity was concocted and got up.

In this regard, complaint came to be filed before the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajpila on 28.06.2012 pursuant to which the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajpipla was pleased to pass an order directing investigation under Section 156(3) of the CrPC and to register the complaint and investigate the offence by the police.
Challenging the said order, present petitions have been filed.

It further appears that during the Tabassum Golandaz vs State Of Gujarat on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146993714/
2 pendency of the present petitions, settlement took place between the parties as the respondent No.2 has received the amount of Rs.17,77,000/- and in this regard, respondent No.2 has also filed an undertaking to that effect.

sentences.text: [6.0] It is necessary to consider whether the power conferred by the High Court under section 482 of the CrPC is warranted.
It is true that the powers under Section 482 of the Code are very wide and the very plenitude of the power requires great caution in its exercise.
The Court must be careful to see that its decision in exercise of this power is based on sound principles.
The inherent power should not be exercised to stifle a legitimate prosecution.

The High Court being the highest court of a State should normally refrain from giving a prima facie decision in a case where the entire facts are incomplete and hazy, more so when the evidence has not been collected and produced before the Court and the issues involved, whether factual or legal, are of magnitude and cannot be seen in their true perspective without sufficient material.

Of course, no hard-and-fast rule can be laid NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/2092/2012 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined down in regard to cases in which the High Court will exercise its extraordinary jurisdiction of quashing the proceeding at any stage as the Hon'ble Supreme Court has decided in the case of Central Bureau of Investigation vs. Ravi Shankar Srivastava, IAS & Anr., reported in AIR 2006 SC 2872.

Further, even the complainant has affirmed the fact of settlement and filing of undertaking by him.
In view of the above development, further continuance of trial pursuant to the mutual settlement arrived at between the parties would be a futile exercise.

Hence, to secure the ends of justice, it would be appropriate to quash and set aside the impugned FIR and all consequential proceedings initiated in pursuance thereof under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C..
NEUTRAL CITATION R/SCR.A/2092/2012 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined [8.0] Insofar as offence under Section 420 of the IPC is concerned, it is appropriate to refer to the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rekha Jain vs. The State of Karnataka & Anr. reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 468, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that, to make out a case against a person for the offence under Section 420 of IPC, there must be a dishonest inducement to deceive a person to deliver any property to any other person.

sentences.text: A breach of contract does not give rise to criminal prosecution for cheating unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is shown right at the beginning of the transaction.
Merely on the allegation of failure to keep up promise will not be enough to initiate criminal proceedings.

From the facts available on record, it is evident that the respondent No.2 had improved his case ever since the first complaint was filed in which there were no allegations against the appellant rather it was only against the property dealers which was in subsequent complaints that the name of the appellant was mentioned.
On the first complaint, the only request was for return of the amount paid by the respondent No.2.

When the offence was made out on the basis of the first complaint, the second complaint was filed with improved version making allegations against the appellant as well which was not there in the earlier complaint.
The entire idea seems to be to convert a civil dispute into criminal and put pressure on the appellant for return of the amount allegedly paid.
The criminal Courts are not meant to be used for settling scores or pressurise parties to settle civil disputes.
Wherever ingredients of criminal offences are made out, criminal courts have to take cognizance.
The complaint in question on the basis of which F.I.R. was registered was filed nearly three years after the last date fixed for registration of the sale deed.
Allowing the proceedings to continue would be an abuse of process of the Court."

They have performed their official duty as members of the committee and whatever allegations made in the impugned complaint are against petitioners of Special Criminal Application No.2092/2012 i.e. accused Nos.7 and 6 and after settlement, they have paid the amount to respondent No.2.
